clue.text: Wearing extravagant clothes on HP, say

parts.note: on and over both mean above or upon
HP is a British brand of brown sauce, a dressing for food

explanation.surface: Someone dressed too lavishly while buying on hire purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'HP' looks like hire purchase, the British term for buying on credit; it is HP Sauce, a popular British brown sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdressing is putting on clothes far grander than the occasion needs.

clue.text: Rendering surface of villa, taking ages, brought about injury

indicators.note: the surface of a word is its outermost, first letter
brought about means placed around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: an eon is an age, a vast span of time
RSI is repetitive strain injury

explanation.surface: Plastering a villa takes ages and causes an injury along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rendering' looks like plastering a wall, which suits the villa; it is the definition, as in a performer's rendering of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendering of a song or text is one version or interpretation of it.

clue.text: Carrier that might get jump start by breakdown service in Falkirk's outskirts

parts.note: a roo, a kangaroo, is a creature that starts off with a jump

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
the outskirts of a word are its outer letters

parts.note: the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British roadside breakdown service

explanation.surface: A car in Falkirk needing a jump start from the breakdown service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jump start' looks like reviving a flat battery; here a roo is what gets about by jumping. Falkirk is a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof rack is a frame on top of a car that carries luggage.

clue.text: Decoy requiring switch of hands to guide

indicators.note: hands are left and right, L and R, so those two letters change places

parts.note: a lure is a decoy used to entice

explanation.surface: A decoy that only works if passed from one hand to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch of hands' swaps L (left) and R (right) in LURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule is to govern or direct, so it can mean to guide.

clue.text: Time of government debates in a flexible way? Confusion resounded

parts.note: supply is an adverb from supple, meaning flexibly

indicators.note: resounded signals that a word is to be heard spoken

parts.note: a daze is a state of confusion

explanation.surface: Parliamentary debate time handled loosely, and the chamber echoed with confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPPLY here is the rare adverb from supple, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Supply days are days in the UK Commons on which opposition parties choose the debate topics.

clue.text: During early autumn period, going topless is foolish

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in winter'

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top letter of the word

parts.note: Sept., September, is the early autumn month

explanation.surface: Going topless during early autumn would be a foolish idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops the S of SEPT to leave EPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept describes someone clumsy or lacking skill, so foolish in action.

clue.text: Look fixedly over inner section of ballet for graceful creature

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: to gaze is to look fixedly

indicators.note: only an inner run of the word ballet is kept, its first two letters and last letter falling away

explanation.surface: Watching a ballet intently for a graceful dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inner section of' keeps LLE from ballet, dropping B, A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazelle is a slender antelope famed for its grace.

clue.text: Hired messengers who become increasingly exposed

definitions.text: Hired messengers who become increasingly exposed

parts.words: Hired messengers who become increasingly exposed
parts.note: these hired performers deliver a greeting while taking their clothes off, so they end up more and more exposed

explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' looks like being found out, but the joke is literal undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: These are paid novelty greetings delivered by a performer who strips.

clue.text: Rent a seaport's blue pedalos maybe

indicators.note: rent as torn apart means these letters are ripped up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Renting out blue pedalos at a seaside port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like hiring, but it means torn, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedalos are one example of small craft hired out for fun on the water.

clue.text: Labour defends supremo regularly ignoring commotion

indicators.note: defends means guards by surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: toil is hard labour

indicators.note: regularly ignoring means skipping every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Labour politician sticks up for the party boss amid uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignoring' keeps U, R, M from supremo, which TOIL then wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great disturbance, which a commotion is.

clue.text: Parisian's ready eagerness to polish off a biscuit

parts.note: pret is French for ready

indicators.note: to polish off means to get rid of, so the letter is removed

parts.note: zeal is eagerness

explanation.surface: A Parisian keen to finish off a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretzel is a knotted, crisp baked snack, a kind of biscuit.

clue.text: Relatively cold island, about one centigrade to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the numeral one is written I
C is the abbreviation for centigrade

explanation.surface: An island that is colder than its neighbours, with a degree centigrade towards the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the west' reverses RE, I, C to CIER, placed after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier is the comparative of icy, meaning colder than something else.

clue.text: Craft loaf to be shifted around part of checkout

indicators.note: around means one piece encloses the other
shifted means moved about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a till is the cash register at a checkout

explanation.surface: A shop worker moving a loaf through the checkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be shifted' rearranges loaf into FLOA, and 'around' wraps it round TILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a fleet of small boats, so Craft, taken as plural, describes it.

clue.text: Piece of furniture joint curator's opening with locks

parts.note: the elbow is a joint of the arm

indicators.note: a word's opening is its first letter

parts.note: locks are hair

explanation.surface: A museum curator's rheumatic joint and hairstyle described in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: An elbow-chair is an armchair, a seat with rests for the arms.

clue.text: Dash back with company car once, after a cocktail

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come after the letter before them
back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to nip is to dash, go quickly
the Lada was a Soviet-era car once common in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone rushes back to the firm's old car after a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A pina colada is a rum, pineapple and coconut mixed drink.

clue.text: Central element of restaurants presented by staff?

definitions.text: Central element of restaurants presented by staff?

indicators.note: presented by means the letter follows the other piece

parts.note: staff are workers, men

indicators.note: the central element is the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: The heart of any restaurant is what the waiters hand over.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the card a waiter hands diners.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill of fare offered by waiting staff is central to every restaurant.

clue.text: Gives a duplicate to policeman that is attending crime

parts.note: a cop is a policeman
a sin is a wrongdoing, a crime

explanation.surface: A policeman given a copy of the report on the crime being investigated.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone in is to send them a duplicate of a message, as with cc.

clue.text: Restraint drops when chatting

indicators.note: chatting is speech, so the word is as it is spoken

parts.note: drops of water fall as rain

explanation.surface: Holding back once the conversation flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rein is a strap for controlling a horse, so a curb or check.

clue.text: Person who orders in cattle when temperature dropped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dropped means the letter is left out

parts.note: Dexter is a small Irish breed of cattle

explanation.surface: A farmer orders cattle in once the weather turns cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' looks like giving commands; it means putting things in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An indexer compiles an index, putting entries into alphabetical order.

clue.text: Casually buy old bed, keeping ordinary twin possibly

indicators.note: keeping means holding the other piece inside
casually means in a careless, haphazard way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Picking up an old bed on a whim for a twin room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casually' rearranges buy old bed, and 'keeping' holds O within.
explanation.definitionFit: A body double stands in for an actor, a role an identical twin might fill.

clue.text: Scottish inventor Jack uncovered rare lab equipment?

parts.note: Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone, was Scottish
J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: A Scottish inventor's rare apparatus revealed in a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell jar is a glass dome used in laboratories to cover apparatus.

clue.text: Dina runs in 200m event perhaps shining

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a 200m sprint is one example of a race

indicators.note: runs suggests letters running loose and rearranging

explanation.surface: An athlete named Dina competes in the 200 metres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shining' is a noun here, as in 'the shining of the sun', not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance is brilliance or glow, the quality of shining.

clue.text: Impromptu pop-up taken to party once

parts.note: a pop-up is an online advertisement, an ad
Lib is short for the Liberal Party, a former British party

explanation.surface: An impromptu online advert used by a former political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad lib means spontaneous, spoken without preparation.

clue.text: Some schoolgirls returned home

indicators.note: returned means read backwards
some means only a part of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A few pupils came back home.
explanation.definitionFit: A dome of snow blocks is the traditional home of Inuit people.

clue.text: Repair marks on curtains

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for marks, the old German currency
curtains is slang for the end

explanation.surface: Fixing marks on the curtains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtains' looks like drapes but means the end, as in death.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend is to repair something damaged.

clue.text: Jawbone hurt after summit accident initially

indicators.note: after means the next pieces follow the previous one

parts.note: max is the maximum, the top or summit
ill means hurt, harmed

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A climber injured in an accident after reaching the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The maxilla is the upper jaw bone in the skull.

clue.text: Jays moved into part of golf course rejecting company of flyers

indicators.note: into means put inside the other piece
rejecting means turned back, read backwards

parts.note: a tee is where each hole on a golf course starts

indicators.note: moved means the letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: Jays flying onto a golf course and shunning other birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyers' looks like birds after the jays, but the company is an airline and its flyers are passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: EasyJet is a British budget airline, a company whose customers are flyers.

clue.text: US actor's gown oddly tried on by Republican

indicators.note: by in the sense of beside, as in 'sit by me', so the rearranged letters stand next to the Republican

parts.note: a robe is a gown

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Republican oddly trying on a gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like picking odd letters, but here it rearranges tried on.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert De Niro is an American film star, of Taxi Driver and Raging Bull.
